scenario: An `on response` body lowers with its rule's types, as the rule's own body does. Rule `plan` calls `svc.read` for a Visit on 2024-02-29 (day 19782), with no `as`; the host answers with `ok: true` on the call's own correlation (`corr_from_call: 0`). The `on` sibling logs `due {v.due}`, a bare Date interpolation ([LGRA.2.9.6.10]), and emits a Shifted with `next: v.due + 1_d` ([RLOW.6.1.5]'s FN_DATE_ADD_DURATION) and `text: (v.due - 7_d)::String` (FN_DATE_SUB_DURATION, then a cast that dispatches on its operand's static type), reading `v` through the capture fact ([LCCO.5.2]). Rule `show` logs the Shifted. Messages: `due 2024-02-29`, `1 2024-03-01 2024-02-22`. The breaks: a sibling lowered with no typing environment leaves the cast unlowered, so the rule is skipped and nothing is logged; were the cast removed, `v.due + 1_d` would be Int `+` on a day count and nanoseconds, and `{v.due}` would render `19782`. PATH PINNED: `dsc.rete`'s continuation sibling context, whose `cx_env` carries the rule's `type_env`, read by `rlow_6_1_5_date_arith`, `cast_fn` and `lgra_2_9_6_10_temporal_text`.
rules_ds:
schema Reply scope ttl 1_h:
    corr: String
    ok: Bool

service svc.read:
    kwarg n: Int
    response Reply

schema Visit scope logical:
    id: Int key
    due: Date mutable

schema Shifted scope ttl 1_h:
    id: Int
    next: Date
    text: String

rule plan:
    Visit v
->
    call svc.read n: v.id cooldown: 1_h
        on response.ok == true:
            log info "due {v.due}"
            emit Shifted id: v.id next: v.due + 1_d text: (v.due - 7_d)::String

rule show:
    Shifted s
->
    log info "{s.id} {s.next} {s.text}"
